deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It continues Riemann's draft 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik', published posthumously among the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' in the Gesammelte Werke (1876). It is a qualitative, Herbart-inspired theory of 'Geistesmassen' (mental masses). Its numbered or paragraph-structured theses are:

(a) Older Geistesmassen connected with a newly forming one are activated indirectly. The activation is stronger the more closely they are bound to it and to each other. This continues the previous page.

(b) The most general effect of an older Geistesmasse is 'Reproduction': it tends to produce a Geistesmasse similar to itself.

(c) New Geistesmassen form through the joint action of older Geistesmassen and material causes. These co-acting factors inhibit or reinforce one another according to the dissimilarity or similarity of what each tends to produce.

(d) The form of a Geistesmasse (the quality of the accompanying representation) depends on the relative form of motion of the matter in which it forms. The text asserts this correspondence both ways: same motion-form gives same mental form, and conversely.

(e) All Geistesmassen forming at the same time in the cerebrospinal system are bound together by a physical (chemical-electrical) process between their sites of formation.

(f) Each Geistesmasse strives to recreate the motion-form of matter in which it arose.

(g) Argument against a separate unitary soul-substrate. The unity and interpenetration of representations is the first ground for positing a soul. However, the specific links and their strengths must be explained by the representations themselves, which makes a unitary carrier superfluous.

(h) The laws are then applied to purposiveness on Earth (organic life, history). Geistesmassen persist after death. To explain the planned development of organic nature, they must enter a larger connected mass, the 'Erdseele' (Earth-soul). There they serve a higher mental life by the same laws.

(i) Analogy for (h). Many primitive nerve fibres seeing a red surface fuse into one Geistesmasse. Likewise, the Geistesmassen of individuals of a plant genus from a climatically similar region fuse into one total impression. All plants of a region thus give the Earth-soul a detailed picture of its climatic and chemical state. This explains how a plan for later creations develops in the Earth's earlier life (continued on the next page).

No derivations or formulas are involved.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there is no mathematics. As natural philosophy, the claims are speculative: the persistence of Geistesmassen, the Earth-soul, and the two-way correspondence between motion-form and mental quality. They are not empirically supported by modern standards.
The argument in (g) is stated as point '1.' but no point 2 follows; the list is broken off with '....'.

results.what: Theory of 'Geistesmassen': persistent mental units formed by neural processes, with association by similarity and indirect activation through connections (spreading activation).
results.modern_name: Associationist psychology / Herbartian Vorstellungsmechanik; loosely, spreading activation in associative networks
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (1820s); spreading activation in modern form to Collins & Loftus (1975)

results.what: Psychophysical correspondence: the quality of a representation is determined by the motion-form of matter at its site of formation, and conversely.
Earth-soul (Erdseele) explaining purposive organic development by accumulated experience of past organisms.

deep.surprise_reason: The text corresponds to the well-known published 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' (Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik) in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke. Its Herbartian and Fechnerian content is documented and discussed in the literature. There is no mathematical content.
